fields.says: A run-row field that is always present with a default is one entry in `RUN_FIELDS` (`lib/dispatch-fields.js`). A sparse field stays a conditional spread in `addItem` and `_archiveItem`, so other rows keep their key sets byte-identical. Six fields were once dropped on one hop of four.
Every exit from the queue except a take archives through `_archiveItem` (`lib/dispatch-store.js`); a new exit must archive through it too.

The wake path is `_planWake` (decide) then `_deliverWake` (deliver) in `lib/dispatch-store.js`, shared by `addFeedback` and the held-wake release (LIN-4373). Its guards (LIN-1059, 1165, 1357, 2297, 4080, 4166) run in an order that matters: change the pair whole, keep the wake suites passing, and update the two census pins (`lin-3134-declared-mint-census`, `lin-4080-addItem-census`) if the write moves.
"This run's PR" is the session's own report: `prUrlOfFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-wake.js`) takes a PR on a report line before the `[done]` `url`, which older runners filled by mention count (LIN-4375).

Two `[done]` posts can reach a decide-then-enqueue at once, so "no row yet" is no guard: claim first, compare-and-set on the row (`claimHeldWake`). LIN-4373 relied on the read and queued two leftover rows (LIN-4375).
A claim whose holder skips is released on every path out (`releaseHeldWakeClaim`). A stamp left by a skip held the re-report forever (LIN-4375 review).

Any session can park `[pending]` on CI and finish on a ci-wake `custom` row (`lib/ci-wake-sweep.js`). A rule keyed on the producing kind misses that ending: read the lineage (`heldWakeHolderOf`, `resolveFollowUpRoot`). LIN-4373 covered eligibility, not the held wake's terminals.

Row-only kinds stay out of `DISPATCH_KINDS` (`lib/prompt-templates.js`) and sit in `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` (`lib/dispatch-fields.js`); kind-keyed maps are tested against both. A new bucket can pull a kind into the round-trip walk, which `OFF_SPINE_KINDS` stops (LIN-4376).

The store knows no leftovers (LIN-4383). It holds a parent wake by `heldWakeFor` (LIN-4373), released by the holder's terminal or `_archiveItem` under the build's guard key, so it wakes once. Leftover wording lives in `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`, bound into the store late (`setHeldWakeReleaseNote`) because most releases have no request; a new held-wake feature brings a hook (`lin-4377-store-knows-no-leftover` counts the word and forbids the `formatHeldWakeNote` import).

A feedback-entry kind is one row in `FEEDBACK_KINDS` (`lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js`) that declares every role; readers filter the table, and its row order is the runner prompt's bytes. A shared constant is imported from its owner (`HALT_MODES`, `followUpTarget`, `NEVER_RAN` in `lib/dispatch-terminal.js`). The decision-stamp set had four copies in `lib/`; the LIN-4455 censuses (`lin-4455-feedback-kinds-table`, `lin-4455-constants-owners`) fail on a new one.
Price a pulled extra like any piece: a cost read that rode along with LIN-4201 landed alone as LIN-4226.

A task timeline lane is running from the page's open session ids (`isOpenState`), never the cost row; a lineage's own `incomplete`, not the shared `lineagesTruncated`, decides "not complete" (LIN-4405, `lib/task-timeline.js`).

A test that dispatches a close-out passes a `closeOut` seam (`resolveProvider`): the readiness guard reads comments for every close-out since LIN-4438, and without the seam it reaches the real provider and fails open, a pass the hermetic watcher catches only in CI.

Close-out readiness has five lanes: the route (`codeRouteOf`), the stop-at state, the task page's box (`buildRunEvidence`) and both guard lanes (`closeOutNotReady`). A readiness rule goes in `closeOutWaitsOn` (`lib/run-closeout-state.js`) and gets a row in the shared-trail table (`lin-4438-blind-read-gate`); gating one lane let the page offer a press the guard refused (LIN-4438).

A reader that classifies by kind routes `custom` before `bucketOf`: `BUCKET_OF_KIND` maps `custom` to orchestration, and `bucketOf` falls back to orchestration silently, so check membership (`lib/wall-clock-summary.js`). `dispatchesOf` turns a missing kind into `custom` (`lib/cost-read.js`): confirm a custom kind from its own row before trusting it (LIN-4426).
A full PR URL's repository and number come from `prOf` beside `prUrlsIn` (`lib/run-ledger.js`), for the task page and measure 1 alike; compare repositories case-blind, as GitHub does (LIN-4439).

A per-dispatch figure (its model, cost or completeness) is the fold's answer, carried through `lib/cost-read.js`; a reader never re-ranks `byModel` itself. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

The Harbour calls read is `lib/cost-read-calls.js` (LIN-4457): `readCalls`, `appCallsOf` and `callsSurfaceOf` are pure over docs their caller keys to one workspace (`listInHorizon(urlKey)`). The instance-wide boundary is the `urlKey` / `instanceWide` guard on `lineageRecords` and `readCost` (LIN-4226), not these readers. A new calls shape goes beside them, and `appCallsOf([])` is the one empty shape.

`lib/dispatch-wake.js`: `reportedPrUrlOf` and SD's `sessionPrs` pick a PR by one order, linked only by a comment; changing one moves a PR link. (Drift & Coherence Review, 10 Nov; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-10.md`.)

`lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`: a death between `claimHeldWake` and the enqueue, or a failed release write, leaves the wake held. No sweep: a lease sees no re-report, a sweep scans history, and clearing stamps reopens LIN-4375's double queue. (LIN-4377.)
`lib/dispatch-store.js`: `addFeedback` takes one `wakeHook`; a second held-wake feature first needs composable hooks. (Operator, LIN-4377.)
`lib/runner-kit/contract.json`: the row-shape rule is written twice (`checkRowShape`; SD's `columnProblems`); `CONTRACT_SHA256` pins the bytes, not the rule. (Operator, LIN-4377.)

`lib/runner-kit/contract.json`: no row pins a follow-up to a finished, unhalted session (rows cover pause and stop), though the leftover step resumes its build that way (`lib/dispatch-leftover.js`). (Seams & Tangles, 10 Nov.; `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-10-run11.md`.)
`lib/session-summary.js`: do stored run paragraphs keep pre-cutover figures? (Survey tally: LIN-4201.)
`lib/wake-shadow.js`: one wake policy, from the LIN-3257 classifier this shadow records. (Survey tally: LIN-3257.)
`lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`: the per-message transcript fold is here and in SD; one shared fold would turn a transcript into requests. (Survey tally: LIN-4203, LIN-4195.)

`lib/recent-runs.js`: `runFact` reads only the row's feedback: a stage parked `[pending]` whose lineage ends `[blocked]` or `[skipped]` reads `running` and holds the live-stage wait until aborted. (LIN-4392.)

`lib/run-ledger.js`: `landingPrUrls` counts every full PR URL after its anchor, so it disagrees with the other landing readers in two cases the shared-trail table pins as chosen, not designed (`tests/unit/lin-4438-blind-read-gate.test.js` rows 14 and 15): an audit report that re-cites a merged landing PR puts it in the notes PR's landing (`auditAfterLandingCloseOut` in `lib/recommendation-facts.js` treats only the new PR as the notes PR), and a foreign PR cited before the first review joins a first landing. Each costs a read that must name an extra PR. One comment classifier and one landing reader would make both follow from one rule. A third case is not pinned: an agent's own note (first line `autopilot`, `plan posted`, `plan revised`, or `revision N`) that cites a new PR after review joins `landingPrUrls` but not `isLandingEvidence` (`lib/recommendation-facts.js`), so `blindReadStep` offers a blind read naming a PR the approved review never covered, where a plain note sends it back to review (reproduced at e2d4659c4; Seams & Tangles, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-13-run12.md`, §3.0a). (LIN-4438; Survey global on LIN-4438.)

`lib/run-ledger.js`: `landingPrUrls` skips only blind reads and survey reports, so a comment headed `## Area read` that names a full PR URL would join the ticket's landing. Only the prose rule in `docs/plans/survey/area-read.md` (cite `path@sha`, never a PR URL) keeps the LIN-4447 area reads out today. An area-read kind in the one comment classifier (LIN-4458, piece 2) would make that rule code. (Leftover of LIN-4453; Survey global on LIN-4453.)

`lib/run-closeout-state.js`: `deriveCloseOutState` works from two PR lists: `prs` (`extractPrUrls`, every PR ever cited) drives the PR-shape reasons (multiple-prs, partial, merged) and `landingPrs` (`landingPrUrls`) drives the blind-read gate, so the box can count PRs the gate ignores and the other way round (pinned in `tests/unit/lin-4438-blind-read-gate.test.js` rows 14 and 15). Which reader answers "this task's PRs" spans the box, the guard and the route. (Blind read on LIN-4439.)

`lib/close-out-readiness.js`: in the stop-at lane `deriveCloseOutState` lets merged and partial outrank the gate, then `closeOutNotReady` asks `closeOutWaitsOn` again to override it, so the box state is not the guard's whole answer and the precedence lives in two files. Carrying the gate's answer in the state changes the box model the renderers read. (Blind read on LIN-4439.) `ladderNotReady` asks the gate a third time, so the box and the guard order the same reasons two ways and the next close-out reason must be placed in both; one order is a decision about what the box shows versus what the guard refuses. (Blind read on LIN-4396.)

`lib/run-closeout-state.js`: the close-out reasons are bare string literals: `'blind-read-missing'` is spelled here and again in `REFUSED_REASONS` (`lib/close-out-readiness.js`, beside `'head-moved'`), and `closeOutNotReadyRefusal` builds its error by capitalising `state.message`. A reasons constant (like `CLOSE_OUT_STATUS`) covering every reason, used by the box, the guard and the render, would give them one vocabulary. (Blind read on LIN-4396.)

`lib/run-closeout-state.js`: `closeOutSetsDone` never asks `closeOutWaitsOn`, so the owner's check (`routes/workspace-api-run-evidence.js`) sets a stop-at-PR task Done when its landing PR is merged and approved with no blind read, while the close-out guard (`lib/close-out-readiness.js`) refuses the same trail as `blind-read-missing`, and `blindReadStep` (`lib/recommendation-blind-read.js`) then routes a read to the Done ticket (it stands aside on a completed ticket only after a close-out). The entries above name the box/guard precedence split; this is its Done path. Whether a person's own check may pass the gate is a decision; the shared-trail test runs with `byPersonCheck: false`, so it never reaches this path. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov., second read; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

`lib/cost-read-calls.js`: `readCalls` states the figure rule (`totalUsd` only when everything is priced and complete; `pricedUsd` never counts a partial) in its own words, and the lineage figure in `lib/cost-read.js` states it again, so a change to the rule is made twice. One shared helper would make it one, but it reaches the lineage path and its goldens: larger than a fix. (LIN-4457 leftovers; Survey global on LIN-4457.)

`lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js`: the table's `mayCarryWake` column is `true` on every row (unknown kinds pass too), so `findWakeEvent` (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js`) never skips a kind, while `lastWakeEntry` (`lib/run-view.js`) skips the decision-stamp kinds as "never a wake marker". Two wake scans disagree about stamps, and the column only records `findWakeEvent`'s behaviour. Removing the column or making it true to both readers means deciding whether `findWakeEvent` should skip stamps, which changes wake minting and every reader of stored rows. (LIN-4455 blind read.)

`lib/dispatch-factory.js`: `refusesHermeticToken` skips access for a provider that declares `testTransport` (`LinearProvider`, `lib/providers/linear/index.js`), but nothing links that declaration to the transport swaps it describes (`routes/test.js` `installTestTokenLinearTransport`, `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js`), so a new installer or a change to Linear's can drift from it silently. Closing it means deciding where test transports register (for example installers that declare which provider they cover, plus a census test), across providers, web routes and fixtures: larger than a fix. (LIN-4456 blind read, 13 Nov.)

Prompt size is frozen (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`): text grows only with its ticket and reason beside the ceiling and `FROZEN_TOTAL_BYTES`; old reasons go to "Ceiling history" in `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md`.
Grounding lists in `lib/prompt-formatters.js` are shared (`WORK` serves several stages, `GROUNDING_NOTES` unknown kinds): give one stage its own list (LIN-4371).
Keep scoping and both Survey renders byte-identical unless a ticket is about them (replays compare them, LIN-4369).
The Surveys get no area notes pointer: survey-place reads no shape reports, which feed the notes. Scoping cites its pointer in its final message; both share `AREA_NOTES_WHERE` (LIN-4346).

`lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and the budget test change in almost every merge: rebase, then re-measure. Its fixture passes no context (the empty-context branch), so dropping one can raise a ceiling while real renders shrink (LIN-4393).
The `## As asked` block's words have one owner, `lib/as-asked.js`: import its spellings, never retype the heading or end line (LIN-4362).

`lib/prompt-template-defs.js` cannot import what imports `lib/prompt-templates.js` (a cycle): shared words live in an import-free leaf, as `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` (LIN-4376) and `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js` (never restate a rank; LIN-4382).

Prompt words banning a kind of how do not hold it (LIN-4369's replay: closing one channel moved it to the next). Hold the shape in code or a test (`SIZE_RECORD_SHAPE`, `lib/size-of-move.js`, arm 3) or hold the reader's side (arm 4).
A stage lead's first sentence is the selector's purpose line: changing it means new router snapshots, `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt` and routing ceiling (LIN-4369).
`lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js`: check real rows reach a server guard before prompt text bypasses it (LIN-4349). A scoped run's Periodical is opt-in by goal: no tail, no flag (LIN-4415).

`lib/periodicals.js`: close-out merges a Periodical's PR and sets Done as for any task; give no Periodical its own merge rule: notes are prompt input (LIN-4390). The rule is retyped in five files; only a test links them.
Model facts come from the OpenRouter catalog: add no model list or rate (LIN-4358); tests seed `tests/unit/helpers/pinned-catalog.js`.

`lib/library.js` takes a shelf doc's summary by position (`firstParagraphAfterTitle`): a paper that opens with a figure keeps its alt text under 12 words, or the alt text becomes the summary; a rewritten first paragraph re-pins `tests/fixtures/library-doc-summaries.json` (LIN-4428).

A blind reader's limits are instructions, not access: with the repository checked out it can still see commit subjects (`git worktree add` prints the head's) and area notes. Both slipped, harmlessly, in the LIN-4436 pilot. Code hands a blind stage SHAs and PR URLs, never a PR body or commit log.

`lib/periodicals.js`: Stability defers to a repo's committed declaration of its measures and names none (LIN-4424): change Harbour's measures in `docs/reviews/stability-measures/README.md` and its script, never in the shared template; a test links the bullet's list to that README.

A new stage kind is a row in every table `tests/unit/stage-kind-tables.test.js` reads: add it, or list it there as out with the reason. A kind in `SPINE` (`lib/run-view.js`) also moves the run page's "n of N", the session and task-page goldens (`UPDATE_RENDER_SESSION_GOLDEN=1`, `UPDATE_RENDER_TASK_PAGE_GOLDEN=1`) and the E2E count pins; read the golden diff before accepting it (LIN-4437).

`formatCiGateCheck` (`lib/prompt-formatters.js`) renders in implementation, review and close-out: a rule for one stage gets its own formatter beside it. Prove the others unchanged by rendering every kind, fresh and fix round, at HEAD and on the branch, not by the budget test, whose ceilings are caps (LIN-4441).

`lib/recommendation-input.js`: the pinned-kind and in-app renders (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, `routes/proxy-compute.js` twice, `routes/workspace-api-prompts.js`) build context by hand: a new field must reach all five (LIN-4368 missed one; LIN-4393 leftovers.)
`lib/size-of-move.js`: the built-in policy (`DECIDED_BY.policy`, err larger) may stand in for John's "per task breakdown of options"; its size words are unexplained. (John, LIN-4393.)

`lib/prompts/stage-intent.js`: `CUT` writes the closing contract's token order (`DECISION:` before `BLOCKED:`) into a scope line beside `ASK`. Its "cut" and the plan-review and review "narrowing" (`lib/completion-signals.js`) name one thing; no test links them. (John, 8 Nov.)

`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`: a stage kind is a row in ~fourteen parallel tables (`GROUNDING_BY_KIND`, ceilings, completion signals, labels…): fold them into one definition. (Survey tally, LIN-4248.)

`lib/call-budget.js`: the budget rule is untested live on anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5; before moving a call there, replay LIN-4352's snapshot through `scripts/replay-brief.mjs`: block [2] WHOLE, four sections, finishReason=stop, any retry's reasoning bound accepted. REFUSED: change the rule first. (John, LIN-4358.)

`lib/call-budget.js`: split: `resolveReasoningBudget`/`isReasoningModel` stay in `lib/openrouter.js`; tool hops and the routing pair get the budget, not the retry; `canReason` has test callers only. (Area reads CG/CH.)

`lib/openrouter.js`: `SUGGESTED_MODEL_IDS` and `DISPATCH_MODEL_SUGGESTIONS` (`lib/model-routing-harnesses.js`) repeat ids by hand, unchecked; the first is also the cold-catalog fallback. (Area reads CG/CH.)

`lib/periodicals.js`: `docs/areas/` is spelled in 26 lines across 11 code files (`lib/`, `routes/`, `public/`, `server.js`, `scripts/`), up from 17 in 10 at the 10 Nov reading, and two leaves now spell the directory: `REGISTRY_PATH` (`lib/prompts/area-registry-path.js`) and `NOTES_DIR` (`lib/prompts/area-note-format.js`, LIN-4420), neither derived from the other. Moving the notes means editing both leaves and the prose. (Drift & Coherence Review, 10 Nov; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-10.md`; count, Documentation Review; recounted, Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)
`lib/recommendation-live-wait.js`: a read, not a claim: two different-kind calls racing on one ticket both pass; claim compare-and-set, like `claimHeldWake` (LIN-4392).

`lib/recommendation-live-wait.js`: the live-stage refusal (`liveWaitRefusal`, 409 `STAGE_IN_FLIGHT`) is a Runs dispatch rule placed here by the `^lib/recommendation-` prefix. `lib/dispatch-entrance.js` (Runs) enforces it, `routes/workspace-api.js` (Web) imports it, `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (Agent API) takes its code, and the one run-state test it makes, `isLiveRun`, is in `lib/recent-runs.js` (Runs), so a change to what counts as live moves three areas. `lib/openrouter.js` (LLM) also routes on it, as the first code-settled route in `codeRouteOf`, so the wait is recommendation logic as well. A size of move: give the wait a Runs home. (Seams & Tangles, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-13-run12.md`.)

`lib/periodicals.js`: two sizes of move: a ceiling for Periodical prompts (+18.8% in the window, 185,952 to 220,882 B; only a sha256 tripwire), and an index or series archive for `docs/reviews/` (109 top-level reports, 88 MB). (Documentation Review, 10 Nov.; `docs/reviews/documentation-review-2026-11-10.md`.)

`lib/prompt-formatters.js`: eight stage kinds are told notes bind, yet `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` checks shape only and close-out writes review-worded entries to main unreviewed: no content boundary on who adds a Lesson. (Security Review, 10 Nov.; `docs/reviews/security-review-2026-11-10.md`.)

`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`: a dispatch holder's `goal` is "Goal from the human" (ranked first), a periodical mint `note` "the operator" (`lib/periodicals.js`): attribute both to the minting token. (Security Review, 10 Nov.; `docs/reviews/security-review-2026-11-10.md`.)

`lib/library.js`: summaries come from first-paragraph position, so an opening image's alt text can become the summary and every shelf rewrite churns `tests/fixtures/library-doc-summaries.json`; a `summary:` front-matter field would end both, but changes every doc's summary source. (Survey global, LIN-4428.)

`lib/periodicals.js`: a reading's finding with no file in an area to cite goes to the closing comment, "never in a ticket", a live secret included, while `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` (`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`) sends a find that touches safety to a ticket. The two rules in this area answer the live-secret case oppositely; having Periodicals render the gate needs John's ruling on that case first. (LIN-4401, LIN-4431.)

`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`: since `CONSEQUENCE_TEST` (LIN-4401), outside finds gather as Waiting entries in other areas' notes where tickets used to be filed. LIN-4414's one retirement per build drains only the areas a build touches, so rarely touched notes (other-features) will grow; their Waiting counts are the honest measure. (LIN-4431.)

`lib/prompt-template-defs.js` (retrospective-audit Reporting) and `lib/periodicals.js` (`areaNotesRoutes`) each state the docs-only notes-PR rule in their own words; one shared constant in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` would make it one, at the cost of re-pinning the 13 Periodical prompt hashes. (LIN-4432.)

`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`: the first-match area lookup is spelled three ways: `CONSEQUENCE_TEST`'s "first match wins" parenthetical, `docs/areas/README.md` ("take the first area with a pattern that matches its path") and the blind-read prompt's own sentence (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, the `blind-read` template), which shipped as piloted (LIN-4437), so it was not retyped after the pilot. One constant in the leaf would make it one, at the cost of re-piloting that sentence. (LIN-4436 leftovers.)

`lib/prompt-formatters.js`: `formatLocalTestRule` names this repo's runner command (`node scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs tests/unit/<files>`) in a template that also drives other repos, and `CLAUDE.md` spells the same rule; a repo-supplied test command would make the line right elsewhere and give it one spelling. (LIN-4441 leftovers.)

`lib/periodicals.js`: "search the repo for a committed tool (no path is written here) and run it" is spelled four times: Drift & Coherence's census bullet, Seams & Tangles' two bullets and Stability's declaration bullet. One shared helper would make it one, at the cost of re-pinning those three templates' hashes. (LIN-4424 leftovers; Survey global.) The rule it answers, whether a review may run a tool the repo commits, is itself worded per template: Stability's run bullet says "introducing no tooling beyond what the repo commits", while Recent Headwinds (which reads the same rework and churn trajectory) and Drift & Coherence still say "introducing no new tooling", Code Quality says "introduce no new tooling", and Seams & Tangles allows committed tools in its own bullets. No `periodicalBullet` helper owns it; deciding it is one rule re-pins every template that states it. (LIN-4424 blind read.)

`lib/model-routing-harnesses.js`: a dispatch record's `model` names the routed id ("anthropic/claude-opus-4.8" for the `opus` route), but the claude-code harness runs a Claude id by its family token (`isModelRunnableOn`, `CLAUDE_MAPPABLE_MODEL_FAMILIES`), and on blind-read dispatches d9bdf6d8, cced07ee and 0399b2e2 it ran `claude-opus-5-5`, so a record can misname the model that ran. Cost is already priced from the model the worker reports. Waiting: make the record carry the model the worker reports, or update the routed id. (LIN-4396 review.)

`lib/prompts/blind-read-words.js`: its header says none retypes its words, but the kind is typed bare in `lib/recommendation-blind-read.js` (the run predicate and the dispatched step), `lib/pipeline-churn.js`, `lib/run-view.js` and `lib/run-closeout-state.js`, and has a second constant, `VIRTUAL_PROMPTS.BLIND_READ` (`lib/workflow-config.js`); `lib/completion-signals.js` types the heading (three times) and the verdict words instead of importing them. The route module does not import `BLIND_READ_KIND` at all, and `tests/unit/stage-kind-tables.test.js` checks presence, not these literals. LOW: a stored kind is rarely renamed; the leaf's claim is what is untrue. `lib/recommendation-blind-read.js` also redeclares `COMPLETED`. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

`lib/openrouter.js`: the four routes code settles (the live-stage wait, the review loop bound, the blind read, the look-first sequence) are listed by hand in about nine places, no test pins any copy, and two are already wrong: `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` says "four routes" and then restates three, without the blind read, and `public/llms.txt` says the blind read is "Sent by hand", where its description (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`) says code sends it. The templates sync test checks that the catalogue bullet exists, not its words. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`: the retirement line's words have one home and one checker (`lib/dispatch-leftover-answer.js`), but which entry to settle (the busiest touched area, else another) and the three forms are restated by hand in `docs/areas/README.md`, simple-dispatcher's docs/areas/README.md, `docs/proxy-integration.md` (with the refusal kinds) and `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md`, and the verbatim guard reads only `lib/` and `routes/`. simple-dispatcher's README says a waiting entry also leaves when "a follow-up is filed for it", where this README says only when the consequence test sends it to a ticket. A cross-repo seam; simple-dispatcher's side is named here, not edited. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

`lib/prompts/area-note-format.js`: the one reading of a waiting entry in code does not hold what a cited path is; that rule is in the guard (`tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`, a listed extension), in `lib/dispatch-leftover-answer.js` (any one to six characters, its comment calling it the guard's rule) and in simple-dispatcher's guard. A retirement line can name a path the guard would not read as one. Borderline. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

`lib/prompts/runner-kickoff.js`: imports `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` from the store (`lib/dispatch-store.js`), the only importer of the store's re-export of it (`export { FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS } from './dispatch-feedback-kinds.js'`). Importing from the leaf `lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js` would let the store drop the shim and keep the prompt module off the store's import graph. The runner prompt bytes and the kinds' exact order must not change. (LIN-4455 blind read.)

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "we've not been applying quite the right force to bend the curve… now want to run both real work, and some real tidies." The Drift & Coherence and Seams & Tangles reviews of 13 Nov found this area carrying rules written in two places that disagree. Batch 1 added several of them:

* Harbour can mark a task Done on a person's check before its blind read, while another check refuses that same task, and a read is then sent to a ticket that's already Done (Drift run 7, `close-out-gate-precedence-split`). John's ruling: "if I choose to do something, Harbour is a passenger. This reflects that for many real projects, they're unlikely to be exclusively changed via Harbour."
* Two pieces of code decide which PRs belong to a task, and they disagree about agent notes, so a blind read can be offered over a PR no review covered (Seams run 12, §3.0a).
* The task timeline decides which model a dispatch used by its own rule, separate from the one the cost figures use (Drift, row 150).
* The check that makes a stage wait while another is live is a runs rule, but it lives with the prompts (Seams, P-LW1).

The area's note holds 20 Waiting entries, and `lib/dispatch-store.js` is 4,530 lines. Seams also tried moving files between areas three ways, and none made the tangle smaller.

**What we want.**

* Each rule in the area has one home, and the copies are gone.
* When a person acts, Harbour follows, and that rule is written once.
* The area's Waiting entries are settled, or each says why it can't be yet.
* Each piece finishes one move and names what it retired. John: "I'd be happy to run a small variety, erring larger, to see", so piece sizes vary, leaning larger.
* The LLM & prompts side of the seam is A14's.

**Done when**

* the cases above are settled, or John has ruled they can wait;
* the area's Waiting entries are settled or say why not;
* the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** The tightest tangle in Harbour is between LLM & prompts and Runs & dispatch: the links between the two areas grew from 32 one way and 50 the other to 38 and 55 over batch 1 (Seams run 12). On this side:

* the list of routes that code settles without asking a model is copied about nine times, and `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` and `public/llms.txt` already describe it wrongly (Drift, row 154);
* the blind read's name and heading are retyped outside the file that defines them (Drift, row 151);
* batch 1 added rules to the prompts as text (the frozen prompt total rose about 21,000 bytes, to 378,915). John on that limit: "That limit is to push against lists if rules. Worth knowing, but not hard and fast.";
* LIN-4350 asks to fold the rules together into plainer, more general instructions.

The safety pass (A5, LIN-4400) found two themes here: merge and read-only limits that exist only in prompt text (LIN-1242, LIN-1273, LIN-3417), and tokens inside prompt text (LIN-1372, LIN-1395, LIN-1408). Both are part of A12 (LIN-4416). The area's note holds 26 Waiting entries.

**What we want.**

* Each rule has one home; the copies are gone, and the docs say what the code does.
* A limit that matters is held in code, not only in a prompt's words.
* Fewer rules are restated as lists in prompt text.
* The area's Waiting entries are settled, or each says why it can't be yet.
* Each piece finishes one move and names what it retired; piece sizes vary, leaning larger.
* The Runs & dispatch side of the seam is A13's.

* the cases above are settled, or John has ruled they can wait;
* the safety tickets named above are closed in code for that reason, or John has ruled they can wait;

## From LIN-4447 (Runs & dispatch): three proposed seam moves, for your reply

LIN-4447's design (comment "Design: LIN-4447 @ 4b5001ddf") moves three things across our shared seam. Its pieces 2 and 4 wait on your agreement, so here are the moves, each with the reason it lands on the Runs side. Please reply on LIN-4447 with **agree**, or with the boundary you want instead. That ticket's other pieces don't wait on this.

1. **One comment classifier, home in `lib/run-trail.js` (Runs).** `commentKindOf(body)` would hold close-out, review summary, blind read, survey, audit report and agent note. At the moment these are split between `lib/run-ledger.js` and `lib/recommendation-facts.js`. `recommendation-facts.js` would import `isAgentNote`, `isRuling`, `isPersonComment` and `isAuditReport` from there. `isLandingEvidence` and `auditAfterLandingCloseOut`'s private notes-PR set would retire into `readTrail(...).landing`/`workAfterReview`. **Fallback if you'd rather own it:** the classifier stays in `recommendation-facts.js` and Runs imports it. Either way there is one classifier, not two.
2. **The live-stage wait moves to `lib/run-live-wait.js`.** It takes `liveWaitOf`, `liveWaitRefusal` and `STAGE_IN_FLIGHT` from `lib/recommendation-live-wait.js`, and `isLiveRun` from `recent-runs.js`. The old file is deleted with no re-export shim. Callers in your area (`openrouter.js`, `proxy-instructions.js`) change their import path only. This settles your note's Waiting entry "`recommendation-live-wait.js`: the live-stage refusal … is a Runs dispatch rule" (Seams, 13 Nov). Your note's claim compare-and-set entry moves to the Runs note unchanged.
3. **`blindReadStep` (`lib/recommendation-blind-read.js`) reads the shared close-out decision.** It would use `closeOutDecision().waitsOn`/`followsPerson` and drop its own `isTerminalState`/`COMPLETED` test, which retires your "`COMPLETED` redeclared" Waiting clause. The file stays yours. Only the rule it applies moves to Runs. This is LIN-4447 piece 1, which also waits on John's R1.

Your hand-maintained code-route lists (`openrouter.js`, about nine copies) stay yours. LIN-4447 adds no copy of them.
